# The graph generated by all singleton-cold ANDs

Take a trimmed binary monotone graph-predicate circuit all of whose ANDs reject all singleton inputs. Let K consist of all pairs on which at least one original AND is true. It contains the target graph G because the output has no raw OR-only input path and accepts every target edge.

Project every wire onto its raw OR-only ancestors by interpreting each AND output as zero. Keep only the ORs with two nonempty projected operands; the others simplify for free. For every original AND with two nonempty projected operands, form their product. Each product is bounded by its original AND. Conversely if some AND fires on a pair, take the earliest firing one; then both its operands are already true after projection on that pair, since all earlier ANDs were false there. Thus these products generate exactly K. Their two shores are disjoint by singleton coldness. It remains to pay for collecting the t retained products into an OR.

Fix one outgoing path toward the old output from every zero-projection gate, using the same successor whenever paths merge. Trace from each of the t retained AND outputs and stop upon reaching the old output or the first nonempty-projection gate. A transition from empty to nonempty projection can only enter an OR with another nonempty operand. The trace cannot enter another retained AND from a zero-projection predecessor, since a retained AND has two nonempty projected operands. Whenever two paths merge before stopping, the merging node cannot be a retained AND or a paid OR, because both incoming slots are reached along zero-projection wires. Thus each merger is charged by a distinct unused original gate. If k sink groups occur there are at least t−k such mergers. Each distinct stop at a transition OR is an additional unused gate, since one operand there is empty and the other nonempty; it cannot have merged two traced paths. All sinks but possibly the original output are transition ORs. This pays at least k−1 more, covering t−1 collector ORs in total. As G contains an edge, t≥1. The result is a flat realization of the entire K predicate within the original gate budget.

For a 17-gate monotone circuit on 9822, K must contain a four-cycle. Otherwise every flat product is a star, different centers share no nontrivial arm OR, and flat cost is at least |E(K)|+τ(K)−1≥13+6−1=18. In particular the sole additional edge of K cannot be one of 01,18,23,25: none of those four pairs is joined by a three-edge path in G. This constraint assumes singleton-cold ANDs throughout and the original circuit trimmed before defining K.
